exclusion_detail: The abstract speaks only of 'identified lead molecules' without naming any. Six hits (3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 11) are all taken through the same follow-up assays (MTT, wound healing, BrdU, PARP-1 cleavage), so rule 2 gives no single compound either (5 and 7 are the most potent PARP-1 inhibitors; 7 is the most effective in MTT).

lead.label: none (3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 11 tested together; 5 and 7 most potent in the enzyme assay)
lead.why: Abstract: 'the identified lead molecules were efficiently impeding cell migration and cell proliferation'; text: 'compounds 5 and 7 proved to be the most potent compounds tested'.

notes: The route is explicit in section 4.3-4.7 (indole-2-carbohydrazide 1 + PhNCS in EtOH -> thiosemicarbazide 2 -> reflux 4 N KOH -> triazolethione 3; then 3 + 1-bromopropan-2-ol/K2CO3 -> 5; 3 + allyl bromide/Et3N -> 6; 3 + 2 allyl bromide/K2CO3 -> 7 (or 6 + allyl bromide); 3 + acetobromoglucose/NaHCO3 -> 4). So 3 = 2 steps, 4/5/6 = 3 steps, 7 = 3 steps. Indole-2-carbohydrazide is bought ('all the reagents were purchased'). If a looser lead rule is allowed, 7 (most frequent best performer) or 5 (most potent PARP-1 IC50 0.33 uM) would be the natural pick. Compound 11 route (8, 9, 10, 11) is 5 steps.
